name: Coloured gel lighting
summary: A white lamp covered with a sheet of coloured film, so that a set or a face is lit in red, blue or green with no natural cause.
how: Put a saturated gel (red, blue or green) over a hard source; use one colour for each zone of the set.
Light the face from the side in one colour and the wall behind it in a second colour from the opposite side.
Keep the key light at one stop or more above the fill so that the colour reads as shadow and as light.
Do not justify the colour with a lamp in the frame; the colour is the mood.

origin.note: Mario Bava lights Blood and Black Lace with red, green and blue gels; colour light is older in the theatre and in colour film.

adoptions.via: Mario Bava uses gelled light in Blood and Black Lace and sets the look of the giallo.
Dario Argento and the cameraman Luciano Tovoli light Suspiria with saturated gels and print it on dye-transfer Technicolor.
Nicolas Winding Refn bathes Only God Forgives in red and blue light.

sources.title: Mario Bava, Blood and Black Lace (1964)
